info.title: Ask Sage Server API — Full Response Reference
info.description:
Ask Sage is an AI-powered platform providing intelligent completions, knowledge management, and workflow automation.

## Base URL
`https://api.asksage.ai`

## Authentication
Most endpoints require a valid JWT token sent in the `x-access-tokens` HTTP header. Secured endpoints show a padlock in Swagger UI / Redoc — click **Authorize** and paste your token once to apply it to every request.

Get a token from the User API `/user/get-token-with-api-key` (email + API key), then send it on each call:

`x-access-tokens: <your token>`

**No token required:** `GET` / `POST /get-models`. A token is optional there and narrows the list to the models your account is entitled to; without one you get the full deployment set.
## Message Format
The `message` field in API requests can be either:
- A single string prompt: `"What is Ask Sage?"`
- An array of conversation messages: `[{"user": "me", "message": "what is Ask Sage?"}, {"user": "gpt", "message": "Ask Sage is an..."}]`

## Key Features
- **AI Completions** — Query multiple LLM providers with a unified interface
- **Knowledge Training** — Upload documents, files, and data to build custom datasets
- **Tabular Data** — Ingest and query structured data (CSV, XLSX) with natural language
- **Agent Builder** — Create, configure, and execute multi-step AI workflows
- **Plugins** — Extend capabilities with built-in and custom plugins
- **MCP Servers** — Connect to Model Context Protocol servers for tool integration

post.description:
Main endpoint for generating AI completions. 
The message field can be either a string or an array of conversation messages.


Accepts `application/json`, or `multipart/form-data` when attaching a `file`. All fields work in either body type.

persona.description: Id of the persona whose system prompt shapes the assistant's tone and behavior.

tools.description: Available tools/functions for the model to use

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning depth for reasoning-capable models; ignored for models without this capability.

system_prompt.description: Custom system prompt that overrides the selected persona's default prompt for this request.

mode.description: Execution mode; set to 'deep_agent' to run a multi-step deep-agent research flow instead of a single chat completion. Omitted/other values run standard chat.

dataset.description: Dataset(s) to retrieve context from (RAG); a single dataset name, a comma-separated list of names, or 'all' to search every accessible dataset, or 'none' for no retrieval.

limit_references.description: Controls dataset retrieval. When false (0), the dataset/embedding search is skipped entirely, so no retrieved context is given to the model and no references are returned - this can change the answer. When true (1) or omitted, retrieval runs and references are returned (capped per model).

temperature.description: Sampling temperature; parsed as a float in the range (0,1], values of 0 or below or above 1 are coerced to 0.0 (deterministic).

model.description: Model to generate the completion; defaults to the deployment default, 'auto' also resolves to the default, and an explicitly requested unknown model is rejected rather than silently substituted.

live.description: Live web-search mode: 0 off, 1 on, 2 premium (paid accounts only); disabled server-wide when live search is blocked.

streaming.description: When true, the response is streamed as `text/plain`: a sequence of JSON objects separated by the delimiter `@|@sep@|@` (not Server-Sent Events). Each chunk carries the partial `message`; the final chunk carries the full envelope.

usage.description: When true, includes model token-usage details in the response.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name (e.g. 'America/New_York') used for time-aware responses; an invalid name is ignored.

deep_agent_id.description: ID of an existing deep-agent run to continue. Requires mode='deep_agent'; the run must belong to the caller.

prior_deep_agent_ids.description: IDs of earlier deep-agent runs whose context should be carried into this one (multi-turn). Only runs owned by the caller are used.

skip_search.description: When true, the deep agent skips its dataset/live search phase and answers from the supplied context only.

video_options.description: Optional video-generation options object, used only by video-capable models.

- A single string prompt: `"What is Ask Sage?"`
- An array of conversation messages: `[{"user": "me", "message": "What is Ask Sage?"}, {"user": "gpt", "message": "Ask Sage is..."}]`

When sending via form data, the message must be JSON-encoded.

post.description:
Executes a specific agent with a message and optional parameters. Supports both non-streaming (JSON) and streaming (Server-Sent Events) responses.


**Multipart only:** send the request as `multipart/form-data` to attach a `file`; the `application/json` body covers all other fields.

agent_id.description: Positive integer ID of the agent to run.

message.description: The user prompt or input text sent to the agent for this execution.

streaming.description: Whether to stream results back as Server-Sent Events (true) or return a single JSON response when false; must be a boolean and non-boolean values are rejected.

variables.description: A JSON object of runtime variables. For file variables, the value should be the filename of a file uploaded via a multipart/form-data request.

conversation_history.description: A JSON array representing the conversation history.

agent_id.description: Positive integer ID of the agent to run.

conversation_history.description: A JSON string of the conversation history array.

file.description: A file to be processed. To upload multiple files, provide multiple form parts with the same 'file' key.

200.description: Agent execution result. Default (streaming=true): text/plain delimiter-separated JSON event stream. streaming=false: JSON envelope (schema shown).

schema.description: Non-streaming (streaming=false) JSON body. Streaming default returns text/plain delimiter-separated JSON event objects instead.

response.description: process_agent_workflow_result output {response, type, metadata, source?, terminal_node?} or {response:<workflow_output>, type:'workflow_output'}
string or object (terminal node output / generated text / raw workflow variable pool)

post.description:
Streaming variant of `/query`, and the exact same handler — it accepts the full `/query` request body as JSON, or as `multipart/form-data` with one or more `file` uploads exactly like `/query_with_file`. `streaming` is forced on regardless of what you send. Note that `deep_agent_id` is read from the form only, so it is available on the multipart body and not the JSON one. 

**This is not Server-Sent Events.** The response is `text/plain`, and the body is a sequence of JSON objects separated by the literal delimiter `@|@sep@|@`. Split on that delimiter and parse each chunk as JSON; do not use an SSE client. A chunk that legitimately contains the delimiter has it escaped to `@|@@sep@@|@`. The final chunk carries the completed response; error frames arrive on the same channel.
